title: ASME B31.3 Pipe Thickness Calculator
meta_description: Calculate minimum required pipe wall thickness per ASME B31.3 for process piping maintenance and inspection planning.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Required thickness t = P D / [2(S E + P Y)] + c per ASME B31.3 para. 304.1.2. Ferritic steels through 482 °C use Y = 0.4.

title: Pipe Schedule & Dimension
meta_description: ASME B36.10M / B36.19M pipe OD, ID, wall t, unit mass W_m, and MTO total W_tot = W_m × L × n by NPS and schedule.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Lookup OD, t, ID, W_m from B36.10M / B36.19M. Hero = t. W_tot = W_m × L × n.

title: Flange Dimension & Weight
meta_description: ASME B16.5 flange OD, T, PCD, bolting, and mated-pair weight W_pair for NPS ½–24. WN hub bore uses Sch 40/STD ID.

formula_json.formulaBasis: W_pair = 2 W_f + W_g + n(W_stud + 2 W_nut). WN RF table lookup with type/facing factors; WN hub bore = Sch 40/STD ID (B36.10M).

title: Fitting & Valve Face-to-Face
meta_description: Look up ASME B16.10 flanged valve face-to-face dimensions by NPS and pressure class.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Valve face-to-face from ASME B16.10 flanged RF tables.

title: Butt-Weld Fitting Dimensions
meta_description: ASME B16.9 butt-weld fitting center-to-end and end-to-end dimensions with matching pipe schedule OD, ID, and wall.

formula_json.formulaBasis: 90° LR A = 1.5 × NPS(in) = 38.1 × NPS(mm basis). SR A = 1.0 × NPS(in). Bevel 37.5°.

title: Gasket Dimension & Selection
meta_description: ASME B16.20 spiral-wound (ID × SE_OD × OR_OD) and RTJ (Ring No. · P · w×h) dimension lookup by NPS and class.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Spiral-wound: ID, IR_OD, SE_OD, OR_OD. RTJ: ring number, pitch P, section w×h. Lookup only — Wm/torque via PCC-1 tool.

title: Valve Cv Sizing Calculator
meta_description: ISA/IEC US Cv screening for liquid and gas: Q, P1/P2 gauge, SG, and catalog Cv,sel headroom check.

formula_json.subtitle: US Cv screening · liquid gpm/psi path · gas absolute P · Cv ≤ Cv,sel
formula_json.formulaBasis: Liquid: convert m³/h & bar to gpm/psi, Cv = Q_gpm √(SG/ΔP_psi). Gas: gauge→absolute (+1 atm), simplified non-choked screening. Adequate when calculated Cv ≤ catalog Cv,sel. Choked FL/xT not solved in-app.

title: Bolt Torque & Tensioning
meta_description: ASME PCC-1 flange bolt torque lookup: B16.5 studs, moly T_table (K=0.13), K/grade scaling, and Round 1–4 star sequence.

formula_json.subtitle: PCC-1 screening torque · B16.5 studs · K & grade rescale · Round 1–4
formula_json.formulaBasis: Lookup ASME B16.5 stud size/count and PCC-1-style moly T_table (K_ref = 0.13, A193 B7). Scale T = T_table × (K/0.13) × f_grade (B8/B8M Class 2 = 0.85). Four-round targets: 30% / 60% / 100% / circular 100%. Confirm against the owner’s PCC-1 appendix.

title: Flange Bolt Tightening Sequence
meta_description: Free online flange bolt tightening sequence generator. View interactive star pattern diagrams and tightening passes for 4 to 64 bolt flanges per ASME PCC-1.

formula_json.subtitle: Star/cross & circular sequences · B16.5 bolt-count helper · Round 1–4 guide
formula_json.formulaBasis: ASME PCC-1 legacy cross-pattern (star) sequences for even bolt counts 4–64, numbered clockwise from bolt 1 at top. Optional NPS × class helper fills bolt count from the same ASME B16.5 / B16.47 joint table as the Bolt Torque tool. Assembly rounds: 30% / 60% / 100% star, then 100% circular check — aligned with FEK torque screening.

faq.q: What is an 8-bolt flange star pattern?
faq.a: Number bolts 1–8 clockwise from the top. Tighten in order 1 → 5 → 3 → 7 → 2 → 6 → 4 → 8 (opposite pairs), then finish with a circular 100% pass.

faq.q: Does this replace ASME PCC-1 Appendix F?
faq.a: No. It is a field sequence diagram and Round 1–4 reminder. Use the project procedure and the Bolt Torque calculator for wrench targets.

title: Blind Flange Thickness
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 / VIII-1 UG-34 flat blind thickness t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c from diameter, design pressure, and corrosion allowance.

formula_json.subtitle: Attachment factor C = 0.30 (B31.3 304.4.1 / VIII-1 UG-34).
formula_json.formulaLatex: t_m = d \times \sqrt{\frac{0.30 P}{S E}} + c \quad (\text{hydro: omit } c,\; P \to P_t)
formula_json.formulaBasis: Required thickness uses t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c. C = 0.30 is the ASME Section VIII Division 1 UG-34 / B31.3 para. 304.4.1 bolted flat-cover factor. d is inside or gasket contact diameter; P and S share stress units; c is corrosion allowance.

title: Metal Weight & Cost Estimator
meta_description: Estimate metal weight and procurement cost for plate, pipe, and bar shapes using material density and unit price.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Mass = density × volume for plate, pipe, and bar. Densities are typical CS / 304 / Al / Cu screening values.

title: Stainless Steel & Special Alloy Weight & Density
meta_description: Calculate weight and volume for SS304, SS316L, Duplex, Inconel, and Titanium plates, pipes, and bars. Includes material density reference tables.

formula_json.subtitle: SS / Duplex / Nickel alloy mass = ρ × V · plate, pipe, bar
formula_json.formulaBasis: Mass = density × volume. Densities are typical catalog values (e.g. SS304 7930 kg/m³, SS316 8000 kg/m³). Pipe volume uses OD and wall; plate/rect use L×W×t; round bar uses π/4·D²·L. Optional unit price screens material cost. Not a mill certificate substitute.

faq.q: Why does SS316 weigh more than SS304 for the same size?
faq.a: Typical catalog density for SS316 is about 8.00 g/cm³ versus 7.93 g/cm³ for SS304 — roughly 0.9% denser, so the same volume is slightly heavier.

faq.q: Are these densities exact for every heat?
faq.a: No. They are screening values for MTO and logistics. Use the mill certificate or ASTM / EN density for contractual mass.

title: Hydro/Pneumatic Test Pressure
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure with St/S temperature correction and yield-limit screening.

formula_json.subtitle: ASME B31.3 St/S stress ratio & yield limit check
formula_json.formulaBasis: Hydrostatic Pt = 1.5 × P × (St/S). Pneumatic Pt = 1.1 × P × (St/S) per ASME B31.3 para. 345.4.2. St is allowable at test temperature; S at design temperature. Default St/S = 1.0; field guide cap 6.5. Ambient CS binding 138 MPa / 20,000 psi. NPS holding-time guide: ≤2" → 10 min, 2½"–4" → 30 min, ≥6" → 60 min. Hoop vs 0.90 Sy is a site check — not computed in-app.

title: Piping Thermal Expansion & Anchor Load
meta_description: ASME B31.3 ΔL = αLΔT with guided-cantilever loop H/W and F_anchor for CS, steam pipe, CPVC, stainless, and Cr-Mo — field screening, not CAESAR II.

formula_json.subtitle: ΔL = α L ΔT · H = √(3 E_h D · ΔL/2 / S_A) · W = H/2 · F_anchor = F_bending + μ W_pipe. Materials: CS, steam, CPVC, 304/316SS, Cr-Mo.
formula_json.formulaBasis: ΔL = α × L × (T2 − T1). Guided-cantilever H = √(3 E_h D · (ΔL/2) / S_A); U-loop W = H/2; F_anchor = 12 E_h I ΔL / H³ + μ W_pipe. CPVC uses thermoplastic α/E/S_A screening. Steam uses CS properties at elevated T2.

faq.q: Does this replace a flexibility analysis?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening estimate for expansion loop size and anchor load. Formal analysis is required where B31.3 flexibility rules are not obviously satisfied.

faq.q: How is CPVC handled vs steel?
faq.a: CPVC uses a much higher α (~66.6×10⁻⁶ /°C) and low E with a thermoplastic screening S_A. Confirm manufacturer ratings above ~60–93 °C.

title: Pressure Drop & Friction Loss
meta_description: Darcy–Weisbach ΔP with Haaland f, B36 ID, Crane L/D fittings, and ΔP/100 gradient. Hero includes L + Σ L_eq.

formula_json.subtitle: ΔP = f ((L+ΣL_eq)/D) (½ρv²). Haaland f. Elbow 30 / gate 8 / globe 340 L/D.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Darcy–Weisbach with Haaland friction factor. Fitting equivalent lengths use Crane TP-410 L/D (elbow 30, gate 8, globe 340). ΔP/100 is straight-only; hero ΔP includes fittings.

faq.q: Are steam and air densities fixed?
faq.a: Yes — typical screening densities. For HP steam or compressed air, treat the result as order-of-magnitude only.

title: Flow Rate & Velocity
meta_description: Pipe velocity v = Q/A vs API RP 14E vc = C/√ρ. CS/SS liquid caps and Safe / Warning / Erosion Risk screening.

formula_json.subtitle: v = Q/A vs vc = C/√ρ. Safe / Warning / Erosion Risk. CS cap 3.5 m/s · SS cap 5.0 m/s.
formula_json.formulaBasis: v = Q/A from schedule ID (B36.10M CS / B36.19M SS). vc = C/√ρ with ρ in lb/ft³ per API RP 14E. Default C = 100 (CS) or 150 (SS). Warning if v ≥ 0.8·vc or liquid v exceeds material cap.

faq.q: What C factor should I use?
faq.a: C = 100 is the CS continuous default; C = 150 is the SS/CRA default. 125–150 is common for intermittent service — site standards prevail.

title: Quick Engineering Unit Converter
meta_description: Convert plant units: pressure, dimension, temperature, flow, torque, weight, and velocity.

formula_json.subtitle: Seven categories: pressure, dimension, temperature, flow, torque, weight, and velocity. Also available from the floating Quick Unit dock.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Exact SI conversion factors. Torque uses 1 ft·lb = 1.355817948 N·m and 1 kgf·m = 9.80665 N·m. Mass uses the avoirdupois pound and metric tonne (1000 kg). Velocity uses 1 ft = 0.3048 m. Mass/volume flow uses the entered density (default 1000 kg/m³ water).

faq.a: The ⚡ Quick Unit button stays on the lower right of every public page except this full converter.

title: Link-Seal & Penetration Sleeve Sizing
meta_description: Link-Seal modular seal sizing calculator: annular clearance C, LS model (LS-300–LS-575), link count N, and sleeve / core-drill ID from pipe OD.

formula_json.subtitle: C = (Sleeve ID − Pipe OD)/2 · Model by free thickness · N = round(π·Dp / belt)
formula_json.formulaBasis: Annular clearance C = (Sleeve ID − Pipe OD)/2. Select Link-Seal model whose free thickness seals C. Pitch diameter Dp = OD + 2·FT (bolt centerline for N). Ideal min sleeve ID = OD + 2·FT. Link count N = round(π·Dp / belt width). Screening ≈ 0.14 MPa / 20 psig. Independent tool — verify GPT chart; not affiliated with GPT Industries.
formula_json.formulaLatex: C = \frac{ID_{sleeve} - OD_{pipe}}{2},\quad D_p = OD + 2 t_{free},\quad N = \mathrm{round}\!\left(\frac{\pi D_p}{w_{belt}}\right)

faq.q: How tight should Link-Seal bolts be?
faq.a: Tighten in a star pattern until the rubber links bulge slightly and contact the pipe and sleeve — do not over-torque to metal-to-metal. Follow the GPT installation sheet for the model.

title: Pipe Coping & Branch Cut Layout
meta_description: Free online pipe coping and branch cut layout calculator. Generate unwrapped flat-pattern templates and 16/32-point ordinate tables for set-on, set-in, and miter branch joints per ASME B31.3 fabrication practice.

formula_json.subtitle: Header × branch intersect · unwrapped cut template · shop ordinate table
formula_json.formulaBasis: 3D envelope intersection of branch OD with header OD (set-on/miter) or header ID (set-in). Unwrapped marking distance S = r_B·φ. Peak-to-valley cut depth Δz_max = max(z_cut) − min(z_cut). Confirm bevel and reinforcement per ASME B31.3 Para 304.3.

faq.q: What is a set-on vs set-in branch cut?
faq.a: Set-on sits on the header OD surface. Set-in opens through the header wall to the ID. This tool switches the envelope radius accordingly.

faq.q: Does this replace shop lofting / CNC?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening flat-pattern and ordinate table. Verify against fabrication procedures and reinforcement calculations.

title: Pneumatic Test Safety Distance
meta_description: ASME PCC-2 Article 501 pneumatic test safety distance calculator. Screen stored energy and personnel exclusion radius for air/N2/He tests — field package starting point for inspection leads.

formula_json.subtitle: Stored energy E to TNT eq. to exclusion distance D — pneumatic test screening
formula_json.formulaBasis: Ideal-gas stored energy expanding to atmosphere (gamma = 1.40 air/N2, 1.67 He). D = R0 * (E/E_TNT)^(1/3) with R0 = 45 ft per lb TNT (~1 psi side-on unprotected personnel). Volume from direct entry or pi/4*ID^2*L. Screening only — not a blast analysis or stamped PCC-2 package.

faq.q: Does this replace a formal blast / AHJ study?
faq.a: No. It is ASME PCC-2 Article 501 field screening for an unprotected exclusion radius. Barriers, stepwise pressurization, and written authorization remain separate controls.
V = π/4 · ID² · L using ASME B36 inside diameter for the selected NPS and schedule. Add vessel or tubing volume separately when significant.
R0 = 45 ft per lb TNT is the unprotected screening standoff for roughly ~1 psi side-on overpressure. AHJ and barrier layouts may require a larger zone.

faq.q: Why is pneumatic riskier than hydrotest?
faq.a: Compressed gas stores far more elastic energy than water. Prefer hydrostatic testing when the code and process allow.

title: Pump NPSH & Cavitation
meta_description: Mechanical pump NPSHa / cavitation margin calculator. Screen available NPSH vs OEM NPSHr for water, seawater, condensate, and light hydrocarbons (HI 9.6.1 · ASME B73.1 · API 610).

formula_json.subtitle: NPSHa = (Ps − Pv)/(ρ g) + zs − hf — margin vs pump NPSHr
formula_json.formulaBasis: Available NPSH from absolute surface pressure, vapor pressure at pumping temperature, signed static head (flooded + / lift −), and suction losses. Compare to OEM NPSHr. HI 9.6.1 margin guidance; ASME B73.1 and API 610 expect purchaser-defined margin. Screening densities and Pv curves — not a process simulator.

faq.q: What is the difference between NPSHa and NPSHr?
faq.a: NPSHa is available from the suction system. NPSHr is required by the pump at the operating capacity (OEM curve). Cavitation risk rises when NPSHa < NPSHr.
Margin is service-dependent. Many continuous cold-water duties target at least about 1.1× NPSHr; hot or volatile services need more. Confirm the project / API 610 purchaser margin.
